protein: Myoglobin (hMb), a monomeric heme-binding globin, assayed as an Aga2p surface-display fusion
readout: Expression fitness score, the log-scale yeast surface display level relative to wild type; the source validates it as a proxy for thermostability against NanoDSF melting temperatures
assay_method: Deep mutational scanning: a pooled library of 10,467 hMb variants built by nicking-strand mutagenesis and displayed as Aga2p fusions on Saccharomyces cerevisiae EBY100, labelled for the display tag, sorted by FACS into bins and sequenced; per-variant read frequencies across bins were converted into expression fitness scores. Mean of two biological replicates.
remark: The mutation labels are numbered against the Aga2p fusion construct and are renumbered here by -136, so that position 1 is the initiator methionine of myoglobin; the resulting sequence is identical to UniProt P02144 at all 154 residues and all 2350 labels verify against it. The 119 nonsense variants are dropped as not being substitutions, and the 109 synonymous variants, which encode wild-type myoglobin through alternate codons and are therefore repeat measurements of the same protein, collapse into the single WT row; their spread of 0.29 log units is this assay's own statement of reproducibility. Not extracted from this paper: the NanoDSF melting temperatures of Figure 4E, which cover ten variants and the wild type, and the combinatorial variants of Figure 6C, sixteen of them identified only as Var1 to Var16 with no genotype in the deposited file -- both under the twenty-variant floor.
